description: cam stop kills the sidecar + cleans all per-session markers; sidecar self-exits when its tmux session is gone so abnormal cam-run exits never orphan it.

officialDocsConsulted.summary: Bun.spawn returns a Subprocess whose .kill() defaults to SIGTERM; liveness for an external pid is probed via process.kill(pid, 0) (signal-0), the in-repo pattern already used by src/supervisor/lock.ts pidAlive. No deprecations relevant to this PRD; the local bun-types docs ship under node_modules/bun-types/docs/ but the dedicated spawn-kill page was not found there, so verification was anchored on the existing in-repo usage (lock.ts, run.ts:436-452).

tmux has-session -t <name> exits 0 when the session exists and non-zero otherwise; kill-session -t <name> tears it down. Both are stable; all cam invocations target the dedicated -L cam socket. No deprecations.

userStories.title: Persist sidecar pid at spawn so cam stop can kill it
userStories.description: As the cam stop kill-switch, I need a durable record of the sidecar pid written at spawn time so that I can SIGTERM the sidecar (it holds no lock while idle) and report the kill honestly without false positives.
acceptanceCriteria: cam run writes the sidecar pid to .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid immediately after Bun.spawn returns, only on the result.created === true branch (run.ts ~line 535-543), using a new exported constant alongside ORCH_READY_MARKER / SUPERVISOR_LOCK_FILE / WORKER_PANE_MARKER (do not hardcode a literal where a sibling constant pattern exists). [oracle: file-assert grep -E "SIDECAR_PID_(FILE|MARKER)|\.cam-sidecar\.pid" src/commands/run.ts src/tmux/ src/supervisor/ ]

performStop reads .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid, probes liveness with process.kill(pid, 0) (the same pattern as src/supervisor/lock.ts pidAlive), SIGTERMs the pid only when alive, then unlinks the pid file (idempotent if absent). [oracle: file-assert grep -E "cam-sidecar\.pid|sidecarPid" src/commands/stop.ts]

When the pid file is absent or names a dead pid, performStop reports sidecarKilled:false and does NOT call killFn against that pid (no false positive). [oracle: bun test test/stop-sidecar-kill.test.ts]

Unit test asserts three cases against an injected killFn: (a) pid file absent -> killFn not called, sidecarKilled:false, no error; (b) pid file present + signal-0 throws (dead) -> killFn not called, sidecarKilled:false, pid file is unlinked; (c) pid file present + signal-0 succeeds (live) -> killFn called with SIGTERM, sidecarKilled:true, pid file is unlinked. [oracle: bun test test/stop-sidecar-kill.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/run.ts (spawn site ~line 439 spawnSidecarDefault + caller block ~line 535-543; persist pid right after Bun.spawn returns proc.pid). src/commands/stop.ts (performStop ~line 186; readSupervisorPid pattern at ~line 141 is the template). src/tmux/session.ts or new src/supervisor/sidecar-pid.ts for the SIDECAR_PID_FILE constant + read/write/remove helpers; mirror the WORKER_PANE_MARKER (session.ts:488) / SUPERVISOR_LOCK_FILE (lock.ts:52) / ORCH_READY_MARKER (bootstrap-wait.ts:28) pattern. Gotcha (lock.ts:38-44): signal-0 via process.kill(pid, 0) throws on dead pid; wrap in try/catch (idempotent). SpawnSidecarFn returns SidecarProcess with kill() but no pid exposed; widen the type to expose pid so the caller can persist it. Architectural crux from the issue: the .cam-supervisor.lock pid is acquired only in the active branch of runSidecarLoop and released in its finally, so an IDLE orphan sidecar holds NO lock; .cam-loop.local.md pid is the supervisor pid, not the sidecar process pid — those are the same TODAY (sidecar host process == supervisor), but the durable spawn-time pid file is what stop must read.

[oracle: file-assert grep -E "SUPERVISOR_LOCK_FILE|cam-orch-session|WORKER_PANE_MARKER|WORKER_REPORT_FILENAME|ORCH_READY_MARKER" src/commands/stop.ts]

Use the canonical path constants from src/supervisor/lock.ts (SUPERVISOR_LOCK_FILE), src/supervisor/worker-report.ts (WORKER_REPORT_FILENAME), src/tmux/session.ts (WORKER_PANE_MARKER), src/tmux/bootstrap-wait.ts (ORCH_READY_MARKER); .cam-orch-session is promoted to a new exported constant ORCH_SESSION_MARKER (see notes) and reused by both writer (run.ts:315) and stop.ts; .cam-sidecar.pid uses the US-001 constant. No marker filename appears as a bare string literal in src/commands/stop.ts: the raw filenames must come from the imported constants. userStories.title: Sidecar self-terminates when its tmux session is gone
userStories.description: As the sidecar process, I need to detect that the cam run host died abnormally (the project tmux session is no longer alive) and exit cleanly within one idle interval, with a startup grace window so the spawn-vs-session-creation race cannot trigger a premature self-exit.
acceptanceCriteria: Each idle tick of runSidecarLoop (loop.ts ~line 1069-1077) checks whether the project tmux session exists via tmux -L cam has-session -t <projectSessionName(cwd)>, using the existing tmux helper (hasSession in src/tmux/session.ts:117) on the dedicated -L cam socket. [oracle: file-assert grep -nE "hasSession|has-session" src/supervisor/loop.ts]

When the session is absent AND the startup grace condition has been satisfied, runSidecarLoop releases the lock (if held) and returns cleanly so the sidecar process exits. [oracle: file-assert grep -nE "sessionAbsent|sessionGone|return;.*session" src/supervisor/loop.ts]

Startup grace prevents premature self-exit during the spawn race: the loop requires the session to have been observed PRESENT at least once before any absent-poll can trigger exit (one-shot 'sessionSeen' latch); document the rule in a header comment on the loop. [oracle: file-assert grep -nE "sessionSeen|startup grace|grace" src/supervisor/loop.ts]

Unit test: with an injected hasSessionFn that returns false on every call AND sessionSeen never latched, runSidecarLoop does NOT exit within several idle ticks (startup-grace branch). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-self-exit.test.ts]

Unit test: with hasSessionFn returning true once (latch set) then false, runSidecarLoop returns within one idlePollMs interval (session-absent branch). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-self-exit.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (RunSidecarLoopOptions ~line 1020-1050; SIDECAR_IDLE_POLL_MS = 2_000 ~line 1053; runSidecarLoop body ~line 1065-1118). Inject a hasSessionFn: () => boolean dep on RunSidecarLoopOptions so tests do not spawn real tmux; the production wiring (src/supervisor/host.ts and src/commands/sidecar.ts) passes a closure that calls hasSession(projectSessionName(cwd), spawnFn) (session.ts:102, 117). The idle branch (line 1072-1075) is the natural insertion point: check has-session before the sleep, and (a) if absent AND sessionSeen -> return; (b) if present -> set sessionSeen=true. Do NOT add the check inside the active branch (runSupervisorFn already runs to terminal); putting it on the idle tick is sufficient because the orphan symptom is exactly the idle-poll-forever case. The lock is NOT held while idle (it is acquired+released inside the active branch at lines 1088-1105) so 'release the lock if held' is a no-op for the idle-exit path; mention this in the comment so a future reader does not add a spurious lock.release(). Pattern reference: scripts/cam/patterns.md 'Sidecar-supervisor invariant'.

userStories.title: Scoped fallback kill for already-orphaned sidecars
userStories.description: As cam stop running against a tree where the sidecar predates the US-001 pid file (an existing orphan from the dogfood symptom), I need to identify and kill cam sidecar processes whose cwd matches THIS project, scoped strictly so no other project's sidecar is touched.
acceptanceCriteria: When .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid is absent OR the pid it names is dead, performStop runs a scoped scan for cam sidecar processes whose working directory matches the current project cwd, and SIGTERMs only those. The scoping primitive is a cwd-equality comparison inside the fallback (e.g. `record.cwd === projectCwd` or `record.cwd === cwd`), not a substring or prefix match. [oracle: file-assert grep -nE "\.cwd\s*===\s*(projectCwd|cwd)|cwd\s*===\s*record\.cwd" src/commands/stop.ts]

The scan matcher is unit-tested: a process record with argv === ['cam','sidecar'] and cwd === <project cwd> matches; the same argv with a DIFFERENT cwd does NOT match; a non-sidecar argv with the matching cwd does NOT match. No blanket pkill cam sidecar is used (the bash literal 'pkill cam sidecar' or 'pkill -f cam.sidecar' must not appear). [oracle: file-assert ! grep -E "pkill\s+(-f\s+)?cam.*sidecar" src/commands/stop.ts]

Unit test on the scoped matcher: (a) cwd match + cam sidecar argv -> matched; (b) foreign cwd + cam sidecar argv -> NOT matched (the foreign-project sidecar is safe); (c) cwd match + cam something-else argv -> NOT matched. [oracle: bun test test/stop-sidecar-fallback.test.ts]

US-003 startup-grace is hardened: the sessionSeen latch is also tested against a race where hasSession returns absent on the very first tick (must not exit), then returns present (must latch), then absent (must exit). [oracle: bun test test/supervisor/sidecar-self-exit.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/stop.ts (after US-001 sidecar-kill path, before the marker removal of US-002; the fallback only runs when the pid-file path did NOT find a live pid). The cwd-scoped scan must be injectable for tests: take a listProcessesFn dep that returns ProcessRecord[] with { pid, argv: string[], cwd: string }; the production adapter shells out (on macOS: ps -eo pid,command + lsof for cwd, OR Bun.$ with the existing patterns). Prefer Bun.$ over node:child_process per patterns.md. CRITICAL scoping rule from the issue: scope to THIS project's cwd; never a blanket pkill cam sidecar (that would hit other projects' sidecars on the same machine). Reaps already-orphaned sidecars the dogfood found (US-001 only prevents NEW orphans). Reference: dogfood 2026-06-17 noted an 11h-uptime orphan sidecar.

userStories.title: Real-tmux + real-process integration regression
userStories.description: As the test suite (the 'fakes lie' guard from CAM-55), I need an integration test against a real subprocess and real tmux on the -L cam socket that proves cam stop actually kills the sidecar process and removes every marker file, and that the sidecar self-exits when has-session misses for real.
acceptanceCriteria: test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts spawns a long-running sleeper subprocess as a stand-in for the sidecar, persists its pid via the US-001 mechanism (writes .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid in a temp project root), runs the real performStop against that temp cwd, then asserts the sleeper process is actually dead (process.kill(pid, 0) throws ESRCH) and every listed marker file is actually absent. [oracle: bun test test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts]

The same file (or a sibling) drives a real tmux session on the -L cam socket the way test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts does today: it creates a real tmux session, runs runSidecarLoop with the real hasSessionFn, asserts the loop stays idle while the session is alive AND has been seen at least once, then kills the session and asserts the loop returns within a small bound. [oracle: bun test test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts]

Both tests skip cleanly (test.skipIf or runtime check) when tmux is not on PATH, matching the convention in test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts so CI without tmux is not broken. [oracle: file-assert grep -E "skipIf|tmux.*PATH|which.*tmux" test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Tests pass (bun test). [oracle: bun test]
userStories.notes: Files: test/integration/stop-sidecar-real.test.ts (new). Templates: test/integration/tmux-introspect.test.ts is the closest existing real-tmux test; test/integration/ensure-worker-pane-selfheal.test.ts (CAM-57) is the closest real-tmux + real-process pattern. Per the issue, prefer a fully automated test (not requires:'operator') because tmux is available in the project's bun test environment (the two existing real-tmux integration tests already run there). Domain fit: tmux has-session + process.kill is exactly where unit fakes pass but reality differs (CAM-55 lesson). Use Bun.spawn for the sleeper (a long sleep), capture proc.pid, write it to .claude/.cam-sidecar.pid in a unique mkdtemp cwd, run performStop({cwd}) with REAL spawnSyncFn/killFn (no injections for the kill), then verify with process.kill(pid, 0).
